items.entity: supports of the Fig. 3 row-1 instance
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only the random sampling rule (1-4 constraints, each a fixed point at a corner or edge midpoint, or a fixed segment connecting such points). The constraints used for row 1 appear only in Fig. 3; the caption gives no boundary conditions. The text also doesn't say whether segments must run along the boundary or may cross the interior or wrap around a corner.
readings: Left edge fully fixed: x = 0, y in [0, L]
Bottom-left (0,0) and bottom-right (L,0) corner nodes fixed
Left-edge midpoint (0, 0.5L) and right-edge midpoint (L, 0.5L) fixed
Half-edge segment x = 0, y in [0, 0.5L] (corner to midpoint) fixed
Bottom edge fully fixed: y = 0, x in [0, L]
Three or four point/segment constraints chosen among the 4 corners and 4 edge midpoints

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says 'fixed points' / 'fixed segments' and Fig. 1 says 'Dirichlet boundary condition'. Neither says whether both displacement components are fixed or only one (roller-type).
readings: ux = uy = 0 at every constrained node (pinned/clamped)
Only one component fixed per constraint (x-only or y-only)
Only the edge-normal component fixed (roller/symmetry type)

items.entity: spatial extent of a 'fixed point' support
items.description: Sec. 4.1: a 'fixed point' at a corner or edge midpoint. The text doesn't say whether this is one FE node or a small patch of nodes/element edges.
readings: Single boundary node (a node exists exactly at 0.5L for 64 elements per edge)
The node plus its two neighbouring boundary nodes
All nodes of the adjacent element edge(s)

items.entity: application point of the single load (row-1 instance)
items.description: Sec. 4.1: 'A single external load was applied along the edge of the domain.' The edge and the position along it for row 1 (x_load, y_load in Eq. 25) are not given in the text; only Fig. 3 shows the instance.
readings: Another boundary node, e.g. at 0.25L or 0.75L along any edge

items.entity: direction of the unit load (row-1 instance)
items.description: Sec. 4.1: 'direction sampled randomly'. The (Fx, Fy) for row 1 appears only in Fig. 3. The y-axis sign convention (image rows downward vs. Cartesian upward) is also not stated, so a vertical component read from the figure could be flipped.
readings: Other random angle, e.g. 30, 120 or 210 deg

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says the load is applied 'along the edge'. Eq. 25 encodes a single (x_load, y_load), which suggests a point load. But the text doesn't give the number of loaded nodes, or say whether 'unit magnitude' is a resultant spread over a patch.
readings: Concentrated force |F| = 1 on a single boundary node
Resultant |F| = 1 spread over 2-3 adjacent boundary nodes (1-2 element edges)
Uniform traction along the whole loaded edge with resultant 1

items.description: Sec. 4.1: f is drawn from U[0.3, 0.5] for each sample. The row-1 value is not in the text and can at most be read from Fig. 3.
No filter, projection or filter radius is mentioned anywhere. Sec. 2 describes only the SIMP interpolation and the OC update; Sec. 4.1 gives only p = 3 and 100 iterations.

items.entity: OC update parameters (move limit m, damping eta) and optimizer form
items.description: Sec. 2, Eqs. (9)-(10) introduce m and eta ('m, eta > 0') with no values. As printed, Eq. (10) uses m as a multiplicative factor and no move limit appears. Sec. 2 also calls the scheme 'gradient descent'.
readings: Standard OC, move limit m = 0.2, eta = 0.5
Standard OC, move limit m = 0.1, eta = 0.5
Literal Eq. (10): rho*m*(-dC/drho/lambda)^eta with m = 1, eta = 0.5, no move limit

items.entity: density lower bound rho_min in Eq. (9)
items.description: Eq. (9) clips densities at a rho_min whose value is not given. Eqs. (1)/(6) allow rho_e = 0, and Eq. (2) already uses Emin to avoid singular stiffness.

items.entity: initial density field of the SIMP run
items.description: The SIMP starting design is not stated. Sec. 4.1's 'initial domain assuming full material presence' refers to the stress/strain conditioning fields, but could be read as the SIMP start.

Sec. 4.1 says '100 optimization steps as the stopping criterion'. Sec. 2 says to stop when the relative compliance change falls below a tolerance or at a maximum iteration count. It's unclear whether early termination was active, and no tolerance is given.
readings: At most 100 iterations, early stop if max density change < 0.01
At most 100 iterations, early stop if relative compliance change < 1e-3

items.entity: thresholding of final SIMP design to binary map
items.description: Sec. 2 says 'a thresholding step is applied' and Sec. 4.1 says the sample is a 'binary topology map'. No threshold rule or value is given, so the binary SIMP design in Fig. 3, and its exact volume and compliance, are not uniquely defined.
readings: Fixed cut-off: rho >= 0.5 -> solid, else void
Volume-preserving: the round(f*4096) highest-density elements set solid

items.description: Eq. (2) uses E0, but no value is given anywhere.
Eq. (2) introduces Emin 'to prevent inversion errors' but gives no value. Emin also sets the void stiffness when the thresholded design is evaluated.
Poisson's ratio is never stated.
Only 'two-dimensional' is stated (Sec. 4.1); plane stress vs. plane strain is not specified.

items.entity: physical side length / element size of the square domain
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only 'a two-dimensional square domain discretized into 64x64 square elements', with no physical side length or element size. This matters only for units, or if a filter radius is given in physical length.
The out-of-plane thickness of the 2D domain is not given.
Only '64x64 square elements' is given (Secs. 4.1/4.2); the element formulation and integration are not stated.
No passive solid or void regions are mentioned. The text doesn't say whether any elements, e.g. at the load point or along supports, are kept solid.
readings: None: all 64x64 elements are design variables
Solid passive element(s) at the load application node
Solid passive elements along fixed points/segments
